> Reproducible in https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/releases/tag/4.5.1.stable%2Bvulkan_mobile_fixes which is 4.5.1.stable + cherry-picks of Vulkan Mobile fixes made by [@blueskythlikesclouds](https://github.com/blueskythlikesclouds) recently ([akien-mga/godot@4.5.1-stable...4.5.1.stable+vulkan_mobile_fixes](https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/compare/4.5.1-stable...4.5.1.stable+vulkan_mobile_fixes)).

Note that this custom build is the one I made for Rift Riff and Kamaeru, which don't seem to trigger this additional crash. But notably it doesn't include the cherry-pick of #114657, so if you have a hunch that this might help, I can see if Draknek can update to the imminent 4.5.2.rc1 including all rendering fixes from #114746.

But Kamaeru and Rift Riff are 2D so it's expected that they wouldn't run into this scene shader crash. Spooky Express is 3D.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114657 shouldn't make a difference for this crash. This happens when compiling pipelines which is independent of descriptor set creation. 

>The stacktrace looks similar to the one seen in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114743#issuecomment-3724777936 for an Intel Mesa half-float support issue, but I assume this stacktrace is just a generic "shader failed miserably" error and we'll need to dig deeper to understand what happens.

It may or may not be similar to #114743. They are both crashing during pipeline compilation. #114743 was specifically caused by passing in invalid SPIRV that was created by invalid GLSL, that was introduced in 4.6 dev. The Mesa drivers just didn't handle that invalid SPIRV gracefully while other drivers did. This could be a similar issue if we are generating invalid SPIRV in this case. 

Alternatively, we could just be triggering a bug in the driver. But its hard to tell from where. Possible candidates are:
1. Shader bug that is handled gracefully by all other drivers
2. Compiler bug that is triggered by our shader
3. Driver bug with loading pipeline cache

Also, do you know if the dev uses any spatial shaders? Its possible they are triggering something with either an invalid shader, or an edge case that triggers a driver bug.

From early analytics of the Godot 4.6.stable editor on Google Play, this seems reproducible in 4.6 too with the editor.
So this might be another app/project that can be used to try to reproduce the issue on PowerVR GE8320 devices.

Additional data point from Google Play Console, possibly a different code path than the scene-shader crash, and it hits a pure-2D game.

**Game:** Wandering Alchemist, Godot 4.7.1 mono, Vulkan Mobile. 2D-only: root scene is Node2D, no 3D nodes, no GPUParticles, no custom compute shaders, no SDF/glow; SubViewports set Disable3D=true. No 3D scene pass is ever rendered.

Device: POCO M7 Pro 5G, MediaTek MT6855 (ImgTec BXM 8-256), Android 16 (SDK 36).

Driver symbol at #06 is ComputeShaderCompileState::CompileUF in vulkan.mtk.so, the driver's compute-shader compiler, i.e. the compute_pipeline_create family (#115435), not the 3D scene-shader render_pipeline_create. Compilation runs on a WorkerThreadPool thread, so it's an engine-internal pipeline (tonemap/copy effects), nothing the game requests.

Two possibly-new facts: (1) a pure-2D game hits it, so the BXM 8-256 driver crashes on the compute path too (2D was expected to be safe here); (2) MT6855 on Android 16 (SDK 36), your list covers Android 10–15. No repro available on my side (single affected device, not in hand); happy to dig deeper if you can point at a specific shader/pipeline to inspect.

@blueskythlikesclouds Any updates on this issue?

We're seeing it as the primary driver for crashes for the Android editor in 4.7.x.

Nope. I was not able to reproduce any crashes on the PowerVR GE8320 device I had access to, but I can try again on the latest Godot version soon. If not, I'll have to buy a phone model that is confirmed to definitely have this crash issue.
